paragraphs.title: The Priestly Families and Their Organization

easy.explanation: The passage names Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar as the sons of Aaron.
easy.q: Who were the sons of Aaron named at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Nadab and Abihu died before their father.
easy.q: Which two sons of Aaron died before their father?

easy.explanation: David distributed them with Zadok and Ahimelech according to their offices.
easy.q: Who distributed the priests according to their offices?

medium.explanation: There were sixteen chief men among the sons of Eleazar.
medium.q: How many chief men were found among the sons of Eleazar?

medium.explanation: There were eight among the sons of Ithamar.
medium.q: How many chief men were found among the sons of Ithamar?

answers: They were divided by casting lots
They were divided according to age
They were divided according to where they lived
medium.explanation: The divisions were determined by lot.
medium.q: What does the phrase “Thus were they divided by lot” mean?

answers: Because more chief men were found among the sons of Eleazar
Because the sons of Ithamar were not priests
Because the sons of Eleazar served alone
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says that more chief men were found among the sons of Eleazar.
challenge.q: Why were there more chief men among the sons of Eleazar than among the sons of Ithamar?

answers: The divisions were based on personal choice
The divisions were arranged through an orderly process rather than personal preference
The divisions were based on the number of sons
challenge.explanation: The use of lots presents an orderly arrangement, not one described as personal favoritism.
challenge.q: What does the use of lots suggest about the organization of the priestly divisions?

answers: He was the scribe who wrote the divisions
challenge.explanation: Shemaiah the son of Nethaneel was the scribe who wrote the divisions before the leaders.

paragraphs.title: The List of the Twenty-Four Priestly Divisions

easy.explanation: The first lot came forth to Jehoiarib.
easy.q: Which division was first in the list?

easy.explanation: The eighth lot came forth to Abijah.
The twenty-fourth lot came forth to Maaziah.

medium.explanation: Jedaiah was the second division, after Jehoiarib.

answers: They came to the house of the LORD according to their appointed order
They came to build the house of the LORD
They came to the house of the LORD only on one day
medium.explanation: The divisions served in the house of the LORD according to their appointed arrangement.
medium.q: What does “to come into the house of the LORD, according to their manner” mean?

challenge.explanation: The list extends from the first division to the twenty-fourth.
challenge.q: How many priestly divisions are listed from the first to the last?

challenge.explanation: The verses present the divisions in the order determined by the lots.
challenge.q: What determined the order of the divisions?

answers: According to the number of family members
According to their manner or appointed order
According to the king's choice each day
challenge.explanation: They were to come into the house of the LORD according to their manner, or appointed order.
challenge.q: According to what were the divisions to come into the house of the LORD?

paragraphs.title: Levitical Families from Amram, Rehabiah, and Izhar

easy.explanation: Shubael is listed among the sons of Amram.
The passage says that Isshiah was first among the sons of Rehabiah.
easy.q: Who was the first among the sons of Rehabiah?

easy.explanation: Shelomoth is listed among the Izharites.
easy.q: Who was listed among the Izharites?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “of the sons of Shubael; Jehdeiah.”
medium.q: Who was the son of Shubael?

answers: A list of the kings of Israel
A list of Levitical families and their descendants
A list of the cities of the priests
medium.explanation: The verses list Levitical families and their descendants.
medium.q: What kind of list is given in this passage?

answers: The first or leading person in the list
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies Isshiah as the first listed among the sons of Rehabiah.
medium.q: What does “the first” mean in the phrase concerning the sons of Rehabiah?

answers: It turns to the remaining sons of Levi after describing Aaron's priestly divisions
challenge.explanation: After the priestly divisions, the passage lists other Levitical families.
challenge.q: Why can this passage be understood as describing Levites other than the priests?

answers: They were both sons of Merari
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “The brother of Michah was Isshiah.”
challenge.q: What relationship is stated between Michah and Isshiah?

challenge.explanation: The passage says, “of the sons of Isshiah; Zechariah.”
challenge.q: Who was the son of Isshiah?

paragraphs.title: The Families of Merari and Their Descendants

easy.explanation: The passage names Mahli and Mushi as the sons of Merari.
easy.q: Who were the sons of Merari named at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Eleazar had no sons.
The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
easy.q: Who were the sons of Mushi?

medium.explanation: The passage lists Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri in connection with Jaaziah.
medium.q: Who were listed among the sons of Jaaziah?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “the son of Kish was Jerahmeel.”
medium.q: Who was the son of Kish?

answers: They were arranged according to their ancestral families
They were arranged according to their cities
They were arranged according to their tools
medium.explanation: The Levites were listed according to the houses or families of their fathers.
medium.q: What does “after the house of their fathers” indicate?

answers: Eleazar was not of the tribe of Levi
The list includes family circumstances, not only the names of sons
challenge.explanation: The record includes Eleazar's family condition even though he had no sons.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the mention of Eleazar without sons?

challenge.explanation: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri are listed among the descendants connected with Jaaziah.
challenge.q: Which branch included Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri?

answers: With the sons of Mushi and a summary of the Levites according to their fathers' houses
With the death of Nadab and Abihu
With the selection of the first priestly division
challenge.explanation: It concludes with the sons of Mushi and the statement that these were the sons of the Levites according to their fathers' houses.
challenge.q: How does the passage conclude its list of Merari's families?

paragraphs.title: The Levites Cast Lots Corresponding to the Priests

easy.explanation: The verse says that the Levites likewise cast lots.

answers: David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the chief of the fathers
easy.explanation: The lots were cast in the presence of David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the chief of the fathers.
easy.q: Before whom did the Levites cast lots?

answers: The divisions of the sons of Aaron
easy.explanation: The Levites cast lots over against their brethren, the sons of Aaron.
easy.q: To what were the Levites' lots compared?

answers: Corresponding to or alongside their younger brethren
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates correspondence or matching between the groups.
medium.q: What does “over against their younger brethren” mean in this context?

answers: The Levitical divisions corresponded to the priestly divisions
The Levites abolished the priestly divisions
The priests and Levites belonged to one identical family
medium.explanation: The Levites cast lots in correspondence with the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
medium.q: What was the relationship between the priestly and Levitical divisions?

answers: Correspondence and equal treatment among the divisions
medium.explanation: The arrangement emphasizes matching divisions rather than preference for one group.
medium.q: What principle is emphasized by this arrangement?

answers: The Levites were organized in an orderly structure corresponding to the priests
The Levites were unrelated to the service of the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: Their casting lots shows an organized Levitical structure corresponding to the priestly divisions.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the Levites also casting lots?

answers: David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the chief of the fathers
challenge.explanation: These leaders are named as present when the Levites cast lots.
challenge.q: Who witnessed or supervised the casting of lots?

answers: Both were arranged through lots in the presence of recognized leaders
Both were arranged only according to where people lived
Both were arranged without reference to ancestral houses
challenge.explanation: Both arrangements used lots and were conducted within an organized leadership structure.
challenge.q: What idea connects the organization of the priests and the Levites?
